newsitem.title: UK: Mideast, Caribs clean tankers steady, others soft.
newsitem.headline: Mideast, Caribs clean tankers steady, others soft.

text.p: Clean tanker rates were steady in the Middle East and in the Caribbean but soft in most other sectors this week, brokers said on Friday.

E.A. Gibson Shipbrokers said in their weekly report that although there had been some loss of momentum, "we consider this to be a temporary phase as it would appear that sufficient questions are being asked by the respective traders to maintain an equilibrium between owners and charterers."
They said that after a slow start to the week, an increase in enquiry halted a slide in Middle East rates which have now started to pick up "and we expect will continue to rise in the coming week."
Gibson said long range Middle East levels have increased by about 2.5 points, with 50,000/55,000 tonnes to Japan fixed at about W197.5. and 69,000/74,000 tonnes at about W165.

Enquiry in the Caribbean was steady with 30,000 tonne and despite a good supply of tonnage rates held at W265. On Friday a 50,000 tonne gas oil cargo was said fixed from the U.S. Gulf to India for a lump sum of $1.475 million for Alpine.
The Mediterranean market was slow and soft, with W205 paid for 27,500 tonnes of naphtha cross-Med.
The inter-U.K./Cont market was also lacklustre, with 25,000 tonne cargoes from the Baltic fetching about W200.
But there was interest in shipping product from the Baltic eastwards, with $1.85 million paid for 77,000 tonnes of gas oil from Ventspils to Singapore.
